subject: general
question: The materials through which objects can be seen but not clearly are called ______ materials.
solution:
The correct answer is __**translucent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Translucent materials allow light to pass through them, but not enough to see through them clearly.
 
• Examples of translucent materials include frosted glass, tracing paper, and some plastics.
 
• Translucent materials scatter light, which is why objects behind them appear blurred.
 
• Translucent materials are often used in applications where it is necessary to diffuse light, such as in lampshades or privacy windows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Opaque Materials**

 
 
• Opaque materials do not allow light to pass through them at all. Objects on the other side cannot be seen.
 
• Examples include wood, metal, and stone.
 
• Opaque materials are used where light blockage is required, such as in walls and doors.
 
 
 
• **Transparent Materials**
 
 
• Transparent materials allow light to pass through them without scattering, so objects can be seen clearly through them.
 
• Examples include clear glass, clean water, and some plastics.
 
• Transparent materials are used in applications where clear visibility is needed, such as in windows and lenses.
 
 
 
• **Lustre**
 
 
• Lustre refers to the way light interacts with the surface of a material, often giving it a shiny or glossy appearance.
 
• It is commonly used to describe the surface quality of minerals and metals.
 
• Materials with high lustre include polished metals and gemstones.
